title: Equivariant morphism descent for normalized finite tower splittings
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme, $I$ a small nonempty directed preordered set, $T$ a connected abelian cover tower over $U$ [def-sfb-connected-abelian-cover-tower], and $z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ a geometric point of its covering limit. Let $F,F'$ be set sheaves on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, supplied with objectwise descent data $d,d'$ as in [lem-sfb-connected-abelian-tower-descent-object]: finite labels $A,A'$, continuous $G$-actions, bijections with the actual geometric stalks, and normalized universal sections $s,s'$ satisfying the whole-overlap descent equation and the finite-level clauses. For a sheaf morphism $f:F\to F'$, define $a_f:A\to A'$ by conjugating its actual stalk map by the supplied fibre bijections (with the harmless $\mathrm{ULift}$ in Lean). Then $a_f$ is $G$-equivariant, and on $X[A]$ the pullback of $s'$ along the label map $a_f$ equals $f(s)$. Conversely every $G$-equivariant map $a:A\to A'$ equals $a_f$ for exactly one sheaf morphism $f:F\to F'$. Empty source and target labels are permitted. This assertion takes the objectwise splittings as inputs and constructs neither those splittings nor a global fibre functor.

source.place: Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 5.1.2; Stacks 04TQ and 086J; original normalized-tower proof steps 8--9.

proof.text: Use the supplied normalized universal sections and stalk bijections to define the map on finite labels of a sheaf morphism: conjugate its actual geometric stalk map by the two bijections. This is the real construction labelMap; applying the target fibre bijection cancels its inverse. No existence or choice theorem defines labelMap.

For a sheaf map $f:F\to F\prime$, Step 3 applied over $X$ says $\phi_{F\prime}f|_X\phi_F^{-1}$ is the constant map of its fibre $a:Q_F\to Q_{F\prime}$. Naturality of the canonical double-overlap comparison gives $a\rho_F(g)=\rho_{F\prime}(g)a$ after restriction to each $g$-section. This proves equivariance and naturality of all the splittings. Conversely, given an equivariant $a$, define $f_X=\phi_{F\prime}^{-1}\underline a\phi_F$. Take a common level trivializing both sheaves. Step 6 describes both descent arrows on every clopen cylinder of that level, and equivariance gives the required intertwining equality there (or directly at every $g$ using the same constant-permutation descriptions). More explicitly the $G$-equivariance implies the equality at every finite label because $G\to\Gamma_k$ is surjective by the finite inverse-limit lemma. Gluing gives the equality on the whole overlap.

source.place: Stacks 086J and 04TQ; agent normalized Hom calculation

proof.text: Apply morphism gluing to the singleton covering $X\to U$ and the two given sheaves $F,F\prime$. The compatibility in Step 8 is precisely equality of the two local maps after the canonical identifications on $X\times_UX$. It gives a unique global $f$ with restriction $f_X$, and its fibre is $a$. Conversely equal fibre maps give equal maps on $X$ by Step 3 and equal global maps by the uniqueness clause of gluing. This proves the displayed Hom bijection. If $Q_F$ is empty, the local source is the empty sheaf and the unique map glues; if $Q_{F\prime}$ is empty and $Q_F$ is nonempty, there is no fibre map and no global map. Both-empty fibres give the unique map.

theorem abelianTowerDescentHom {U : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} [Preorder I]
    [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (T : ConnectedAbelianCoverTower U I)
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] {z : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T.cone.pt.left}
    {F F' : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) (Type (u + 1))}
    (d : AbelianTowerDescentObject T z F) (d' : AbelianTowerDescentObject T z F') :
    (∀ f : F ⟶ F',
      (∀ g : T.groupCone.pt,
        d.action.obj.ρ g ≫ d.labelMap T d' f = d.labelMap T d' f ≫ d'.action.obj.ρ g) ∧
      F'.obj.map ((abelianTowerLabels T.cone.pt).map
        (FintypeCat.toProfinite.map (d.labelMap T d' f))).op d'.section_ =
          f.hom.app _ d.section_) ∧
    ∀ a : d.action.obj.V ⟶ d'.action.obj.V,
      (∀ g : T.groupCone.pt, d.action.obj.ρ g ≫ a = a ≫ d'.action.obj.ρ g) →
      ∃! f : F ⟶ F', d.labelMap T d' f = a
